summary: This informational memo defines MIB objects for managing RADIUS accounting clients. It replaces RFC 2620 by deprecating the table limited to IPv4 addresses and adding one that supports version-neutral IP addresses, keeping the remaining objects.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4670 defines management data for a RADIUS accounting client, including counters and the addresses of its accounting servers. It replaces an IPv4-only server table with one that can represent different IP address versions.

subtitle: A RADIUS accounting client management database that supports version-neutral IP addresses.

tldr.problem: The earlier RADIUS accounting client MIB used a table with IPv4-only address fields.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4670 deprecates that table and adds a replacement table with address-type and address fields that support version-neutral IP addresses. It carries forward the other management objects.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4670 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 2620. Its server-side counterpart is RFC 4671.

today: RFC 4670 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 2620. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it; its server-side companion is RFC 4671.

sections.title: What the Client MIB Measures
sections.content:
A Management Information Base (MIB) defines objects that network-management systems can read. This MIB describes the client side of RADIUS accounting, where a client sends Accounting-Requests and a server returns Accounting-Responses.

Network Access Server devices typically perform the client role. A RADIUS proxy can perform both client and server roles, in which case it is expected to support the corresponding client and server MIBs.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB is a set of values that a network manager can read to monitor a RADIUS accounting client. It includes information about the client's accounting servers and message handling.

sections.title: The Version-Neutral Server Table
sections.content:
RFC 4670 obsoletes RFC 2620 and marks its IPv4-only radiusAccServerTable as deprecated. The new radiusAccServerExtTable contains an address type, an address, and an Internet port number, allowing the table to represent version-neutral IP addresses.

The other MIB objects are carried forward. The RFC recommends using the new table as current and retaining the old table only for IPv4-only support or compatibility with older management stations. If both tables contain the same server, their row indexes should match.
sections.plainLanguage: The old table can hold only IPv4 addresses, so the RFC adds a table for different IP address formats. The old table remains marked deprecated for compatibility cases.

sections.title: Counters and Per-Server Details
sections.content:
The module contains two scalar objects and a table with a row for each RADIUS accounting server with which the client shares a secret. The scalars count responses from unknown addresses and identify the client.

Each server row records activity such as requests, retransmissions, responses, malformed responses, bad authenticators, pending requests, timeouts, unknown packet types, and dropped packets. It also records the recent round-trip time and the time since a counter discontinuity.
sections.plainLanguage: Each server has a row of counters showing requests, replies, failures, and timing. The counters help an operator see how the accounting exchange is progressing.

sections.title: Protecting Read Access
sections.content:
The MIB has no objects that can be changed or created through SNMP SET operations. However, server addresses and port numbers can reveal information useful for attacking a server or impersonating a client.

The RFC says even read access should be controlled and recommends considering SNMPv3 authentication and privacy. It does not recommend deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3.
sections.plainLanguage: These objects cannot be changed through the MIB, but they reveal server addresses and ports. Access to the values should be limited and protected.
